## PalmerPenguins

PalmerPenguins [@PalmerpenguinsDataPackage] aims to provide a dataset similar to `iris` for data exploration and visualization purposes. I will be using the `penguin` data set to find out more about penguins:) 
![Penguins Logo](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png){.center}


## Dataset

There are `r sum(penguins$species=='Gentoo')` penguins of the Gentoo species, `r sum(penguins$species=='Chinstrap')` of the Chinstrap species, and `r sum(penguins$species=='Adelie')` of the Adelie species in the dataset. So the total sample size of the `penguin` data is `r length(penguins$species)`. Below is a table to get a feeling of the data.

```{r}


datatable(penguins, 
          options = list(
            autoWidth = TRUE,
            pageLength = 10,
            initComplete = JS(
              "function(settings, json) {",
              "$(this.api().table().header()).css({'background-color': '#000', 'color': '#fff'});",
              "$(this.api().table().container()).css({'font-size': '0.5em'});", # Adjust font size
              "}")
)
)
```
## Bill length 

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
Below a table with the mean bill length of each species is seen. The mean is calculated using the following formula: 
$$
Mean Bill Length = \frac{\sum x_i}{n}
$$

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
library(gt)
penguins_summary <- palmerpenguins::penguins %>%
  dplyr::group_by(species) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_bill_length = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE))
gt(penguins_summary)

```

:::
:::

## Size & FLipper length

```{r}
# Scatterplot of Penguins


ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = body_mass_g, y = flipper_length_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Body Mass vs. Flipper Length",
    x = "Body Mass (g)",
    y = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
